# Requirements Checklist: Core Extensible Platform + RAG Concept Module

**Purpose**: General requirements-quality gate over spec.md -- author
self-review before implementation continues on the remaining tasks in
tasks.md (T022+). Tests whether the requirements are complete, clear,
consistent, and measurable; does NOT test the implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-03
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist`
command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are numeric ranges (min/max/step) specified for every learner-adjustable control, not just some? Chunk size and overlap (FR-004) and Top-K (FR-006) have no stated range, while similarity-threshold (FR-013) does. [Completeness, Spec §FR-004/FR-006]
- [ ] CHK002 Is a minimum or expected count of sample documents specified? FR-010 requires "static, hardcoded fixtures" but never states how many; US1's "picks a sample document" implies a choice among more than one. [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK003 Is a uniqueness requirement stated for `ConceptModule.id` within the registry? FR-001/FR-002 define the contract and the no-conditional rule but never require ids to be unique, and Edge Cases covers a missing field but not a colliding/duplicate id. [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-001, §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the animations/transitions that FR-012's reduced-motion requirement applies to enumerated anywhere, or is the requirement stated with nothing concrete to check it against? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK005 Is a target browser/runtime support baseline documented anywhere (spec.md or Assumptions), given the app is client-side-only and every simulated behavior runs in-browser? [Completeness, Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "per-concept conditional" (the pattern FR-002/SC-002's automated check must detect) defined precisely enough to distinguish a prohibited conditional from an incidental use of `concept.id` (e.g., as a React `key`)? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002, §SC-002] -- Resolved 2026-08-03: FR-002 now defines it as a hardcoded-literal-id comparison, explicitly distinguished from registry iteration/lookup by a runtime id; SC-002 now cross-references that definition.
- [ ] CHK007 Is "clearly documented" in FR-007 ("the code path for substituting a real model call clearly documented at that one seam") stated in a way that's objectively checkable, or is it a subjective quality judgment? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "without external instructions" in SC-001 defined -- does the pipeline's own in-app Marginalia guidance count as instruction, or only documentation outside the app? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "measurably different" in SC-008 quantified (e.g., a minimum number/percentage of differing chunk boundaries), or does any observable difference satisfy it? [Clarity, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "fully readable and operable" in SC-004 given any concrete criteria (no horizontal scroll, no truncated text, minimum touch target size), or left entirely to implementation judgment? [Clarity, Spec §SC-004]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Does Assumptions' "common mobile widths" (plural) align with SC-004's single named breakpoint (375px), or should Assumptions be narrowed to match the one width that's actually tested? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the document-switch reset rule (query/results/step reset to defaults, added 2026-08-03) stated with the same scope and force as the pre-existing chunking-strategy-switch reset rule it's explicitly modeled on, so a future reader can't conclude one is stricter than the other? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Do FR-006 (Top-K) and FR-013 (similarity-threshold) consistently describe how the two filters compose, given both independently reduce the same ranked list? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-013]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK014 Can SC-002's "no per-module conditionals" be verified as pass/fail without additional interpretation, given CHK006's definitional gap? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK015 Is SC-006's "byte-for-byte identical" outcome tied to a specific, named fixture (document + settings + query), or could two different reviewers pick different fixtures and reach different pass/fail results? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK016 Are SC-007 and SC-008 each tied to "at least one shipped sample document" -- is it specified which document/setting combination, or is any combination that happens to work acceptable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007, §SC-008]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for what the Chunking step displays while chunk size/overlap are being dragged mid-interaction (a transitional/loading state), or only for the settled end state? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK018 Are requirements defined for switching chunking strategy AND document in the same interaction sequence (e.g., strategy toggle changed while on the Document step, before ever visiting Chunking), not just each independently? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for the Compare Variants view's initial/empty state (zero variants selected), separately from the one-selected and two-selected states already covered by US3's acceptance scenarios? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §User Story 3]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK020 Does the sentence-boundary chunking algorithm's definition (split on sentence-ending punctuation) address false-positive splits from abbreviations or decimal numbers, or is it only guaranteed correct for the specific shipped sample documents? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-014, §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK021 Is there a requirement for what happens when sentence-boundary chunking is selected on a document containing zero sentence-ending punctuation (a single run-on chunk, or a fallback to fixed-size behavior)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK022 Is there a requirement for whether the single highest-scoring chunk should ever be surfaced (e.g., a "nearest miss, below threshold" indicator) when every candidate falls below the similarity threshold, or is complete suppression to an empty list the only specified behavior? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-013, §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK023 Are accessibility requirements (FR-011) specific enough to distinguish "keyboard reachable" from "keyboard operable" (e.g., a focusable-but-inert control would satisfy the former but not the latter)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK024 Is a performance or responsiveness expectation stated anywhere for the chunking/embedding/retrieval recomputation that happens on every slider drag, or is "immediately" (FR-004) the only stated target and left unquantified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK025 Is the assumption that the current two sample documents remain small enough for SC-006's "byte-for-byte identical" and SC-001's "under 2 minutes" targets validated anywhere, or only implicitly true of the specific fixtures that happen to ship today? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the dependency of Milestone 1's Definition of Done on FR-013/FR-014 actually being built (confirmed via `/speckit.clarify` 2026-08-03) reflected consistently between spec.md, roadmap.md, and AGENTS.md, or could a reader of spec.md alone conclude these are already done? [Consistency, Dependency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK027 Does a chunk with a similarity score of exactly 1.00 remain excluded when the similarity-threshold slider is set to its maximum (1.00), given FR-013 specifies an inclusive (`>=`) comparison? The Edge Cases section asserts the maximum "excludes everything," which conflicts with an inclusive comparison admitting a perfect-score chunk. [Conflict, Spec §FR-013, §Edge Cases] -- Resolved 2026-08-03: Edge Cases now states the accurate outcome (excludes everything except an exact 1.00 match, which the shipped fixtures never produce) and explains why `>=` is the correct, intentional comparison given the default-0-is-fully-open requirement.
- [x] CHK028 Is "at least five named variants" in FR-008 a floor on an open set (any five-plus variants would satisfy it) or does the spec intend the five specific named variants (HyDE, RAG-Fusion, GraphRAG, Self-RAG, Agentic RAG) as a fixed, required set? The wording supports either reading. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008] -- Resolved 2026-08-03: FR-008 now names these five as a required minimum set (not interchangeable examples), consistent with User Story 3 naming this exact set; additional variants beyond the five are still permitted.
